subject: Request: model gating + stable-pin exemption for atlas-mini-v2
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@atlas-ai.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We're ready to proceed with a formal onboarding of atlas-mini-v2 (quantized int8 variant) for the BrightCloud pilot. A few asks from our side:

- We need a stable-version pin for the pilot (to avoid drift during the 6-week trial).
- Atlas has a small runtime quirk: our optimizer emits a fused attention kernel that currently falls back on some older CUDA+cuDNN combos. We understand Redwood's runtime has kernel selection logic — we want to request a temporary pin-exemption so you can route to a compatible variant if the pinned kernel isn't available in a region.
- Compliance: model card attached, and we can share a short compatibility report.

Can you start the internal checks for gating, compatibility, and the pin-exemption workflow? We're aiming for a 2026-06-15 pilot start.

Attachments: atlas-mini-v2-model-card.pdf (pdf), compat-matrix-atlas-mini.csv (csv)

—Ari
Ari Kaplan
Product Ops, Atlas AI
ari@atlas-ai.com

Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Folks — forwarding Atlas' request. TL;DR: external wants atlas-mini-v2 onboarded and a stable-version pin for pilot, plus a temporary pin-exemption/routing fallback because their variant uses a fused attention kernel that may not match all Redwood kernel selections in some regions.

Asks for each of you:
- Dev: compatibility check + guidance on whether we can offer a pinned stable-version with conditional routing to a compatible variant if kernel mismatch occurs. Also, estimate perf delta and cost impact if we route to fallback variant.
- Rohan: runtime/kernel compatibility and whether we can add a gating flag (model.gating.allow_pin_exemption) scoped to the Atlas account/route.
- Karthik: product side — what gating criteria do we need (QA, eval pass rates, regression delta) before allowing pin exemptions for hosted customers?
- Neha: any compliance flags (KMS, logs, retention) for an exemption that allows routing to slightly different binary kernels/variants?

Pilot target: 2026-06-15. Please respond with technical blockers and a proposed checklist by end of day Friday (2026-06-05).

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Grace / team,

Quick notes after initial review of the attachments (compat matrix + model card):

- Compatibility: atlas-mini-v2 is architecturally close to Llama-style attention layers, but the fused-attn kernel they mention replaces a couple of operator boundaries. On current runtime builds (v3.8.x) we have a fallback path that runs the unfused ops but with a ~15–25% latency penalty for short sequences.
- Pinning: we can create a stable pin (model_version: atlas-mini-v2@202606) for the pilot. However, a strict pin with no fallback will fail in regions where the optimized fused kernel isn't built for available hardware (notably older gpus in ap-southeast-2).
- Suggested approach: allow a scoped pin with an explicit 'allow_fallback' flag. Policy: route to pinned binary if kernel matches; otherwise route to verified fallback variant (unfused ops). We'll track token-level mismatch metrics.

Action items for infra/ops: need a quick compat test matrix across our fleet (I'll attach a script). Rohan — can you run the matrix across canaries and strip a perf table? Also need to know if the fallback increases token cost for the customer — we'll estimate.

Attachments: compat-run-script.sh (sh)

—Dev
From: rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Thanks — started the compat sweep on our canary fleet (us-west1 + eu-west3 + ap-southeast-2). Early signals:

- us-west1 (latest CUDA + patched kernels): fused-attn binary runs fine; latency nominal.
- eu-west3: two node pools where the fused kernel currently falls back; unfused path shows ~18% p50 increase for 1–2k token requests.
- ap-southeast-2: older GPUs in one regional cluster do not have the specialized kernel build; fallback works but with 20–30% p99 regressions for long sequence (>2k) workloads.

Operational note: we can expose a routing policy that prefers pinned binary when available and falls back to verified unfused variant otherwise. We should add a warning to the pinned-version UI that a pin-exemption implies possible perf variance and token-cost delta.

Attached: compat-summary-20260604.csv (csv) and a short kernel-compat checklist.

Requesting product to confirm gating thresholds (e.g., max allowed delta p50/p99, eval pass rate >= 97%). Also, Neha — if routing crosses a region with differing audit/logging configurations, we should call that out.

—Rohan
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Thanks team — proposed gating criteria from product side:

1) Eval coverage: model must pass our regression harness on 3 canonical workloads (conversational, summarization, code-completion) with <= 1.5% quality delta vs. baseline.
2) Perf: scoped p50 delta <= 20% and p99 delta <= 25% for expected pilot sequences. If fallback exceeds this, we require an explicit customer acknowledgment and pricing adjustment.
3) Security/compliance: Neha to sign off that KMS+audit trail is intact for any region the routing may use.
4) Rollout plan: canary (5% traffic) for 24 hours, then 25% for 48 hours, full ramp if no regressions.

If infra confirms we can expose 'allow_fallback' with clear signals and we can show per-route cost deltas, I can approve a scoped pin exemption for the 6-week pilot. Otherwise, we should offer a variant pin (atlas-mini-v2-unfused) as an alternative.

Karthik
Product Manager — Model Rollouts
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Quick compliance checklist:

- KMS: Atlas will use their own customer-managed key for payload encryption at rest — we need to ensure the pinned routing does not inadvertently log or key-wrap in a region without the customer's key policy.
- Audit logs: all fallback decisions must be recorded with: timestamp, chosen-binary, node-id, and exact token count. This is non-negotiable for enterprise signed pilots.
- Data residency: if routing crosses regions with different data residency constraints, we must surface that to the customer and get explicit written consent.

If infra/product implement the 'allow_fallback' flag, mark it as conditional on: (a) per-route audit metadata, (b) customer KMS binding verified, (c) signed exemption doc. I attached a template exemption doc (stable-pin-exemption-request.docx) for legal to start.

I'll give final sign-off once infra uploads the compat summary and we have a canonical eval report linked in INF-4123.

—Neha
Head of Security & Compliance
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@atlas-ai.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas request: onboard atlas-mini-v2 + stable pin exemption

Ari / Atlas team — thanks for the patience. Internal summary and next steps:

- We've validated technical feasibility: infra will expose an allow_fallback routing flag that prefers pinned binary and will route to a verified unfused variant when the fused kernel is unavailable. Compatibility sweep attached in INF-4123.
- Product (Karthik) provided gating thresholds (eval + perf) — we need atlas to run our regression harness or allow us to run it against a small sample subset.
- Compliance (Neha) requires KMS binding and signed pin-exemption doc prior to pilot traffic.

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-06-07: infra posts full compat report and cost delta estimate.
- 2026-06-09: Atlas signs the stable-pin-exemption doc and grants access to a 10k-sample eval dataset OR allows Redwood to run evals.
- 2026-06-12: canary rollout (5%) if all checks pass.
- 2026-06-15: target pilot start at 25% traffic.

If this works for you, Ari — I'll send the exemption doc and a short onboarding checklist to your legal and ops contacts.
